terms.definition: A process that occupies the terminal and blocks all other input until it completes. You see its output live and can interact with it.
terms.example: Running 'sleep 10' — the terminal is frozen for 10 seconds

terms.definition: A process that runs independently of the terminal. Adding & at the end of a command sends it to the background, freeing the terminal immediately.
terms.example: 'sleep 10 &' — terminal is free while sleep runs

terms.definition: A shell operator placed at the end of a command to run it as a background process. Linux returns the Job ID and Process ID immediately.
terms.example: 'sudo yum install docker -y > install.log &'

terms.definition: A sequential number (1, 2, 3...) assigned by the current shell session to track background jobs. Local to your terminal session only.
terms.example: [1] shown when you run a command with &

terms.definition: A unique system-wide number assigned by the OS kernel to identify a running process. Unique across the entire system at any given moment.
terms.example: 4823 shown alongside Job ID when starting a background process

terms.definition: A shell command that lists all background jobs in the current terminal session, showing their job IDs and current status.
terms.example: Running 'jobs' shows [1]+ Running sleep 30 &

terms.definition: A command that brings a background or suspended job to the foreground. Used with the job number: fg %1 brings job 1 to foreground.
terms.example: 'fg %1' to continue interacting with a paused download

terms.definition: A command that resumes a suspended job and runs it in the background. Used after Ctrl+Z suspends a foreground process.
terms.example: Press Ctrl+Z to pause a process, then 'bg %1' to run it in background

terms.definition: A command showing all running processes for all users including daemon processes. 'a' = all users, 'u' = user info, 'x' = include daemons.
terms.example: 'ps aux' to see all processes including Docker and system daemons

terms.definition: A field in 'ps aux' output showing the current state of a process using codes like R (running), S (sleeping), T (stopped), Z (zombie).
terms.example: Sl+ means: Sleeping, multi-threaded, in foreground

terms.definition: A process that has completed execution but has not been removed from the process table because its parent process has not called wait().
terms.example: A script that launched child processes but crashed before cleaning them up

terms.definition: A long-running background service process not attached to any terminal. Examples include web servers, database engines, and the Docker service.
terms.example: The nginx web server runs as a daemon on port 80

terms.definition: The command-line tool for managing systemd services on modern Linux. Used to start, stop, restart, enable, and check the status of services.
terms.example: 'sudo systemctl start docker' to start Docker right now

terms.definition: Configures a service to start automatically every time the system boots. Does not start the service immediately.
terms.example: 'sudo systemctl enable nginx' so nginx starts after every EC2 reboot

terms.definition: A tool that handles installing, updating, and removing software packages on Linux. It talks to repositories to fetch verified packages.
terms.example: yum, dnf, apt are package managers for different Linux distros

terms.definition: A trusted online server from which a package manager downloads and verifies software packages. Like a Play Store for Linux.
terms.example: When you run 'yum install git', YUM fetches git from Amazon Linux repositories

terms.definition: Yellowdog Updater Modified — the package manager for Amazon Linux, Amazon Linux 2, CentOS, and RHEL 7. Command: sudo yum install <package>.
terms.example: 'sudo yum install git -y' on Amazon Linux EC2

terms.definition: Dandified YUM — the next-generation package manager for Amazon Linux 2023, RHEL 8+, and Fedora. Replaces YUM in newer distros.
terms.example: 'sudo dnf install docker -y' on Amazon Linux 2023

terms.definition: Advanced Package Tool — the package manager for Ubuntu and Debian Linux distributions. Command: sudo apt install <package>.
terms.example: 'sudo apt install docker.io -y' on an Ubuntu EC2 instance

terms.definition: SSH File Transfer Protocol — a secure file transfer protocol that runs over SSH on port 22, encrypting both commands and data.
terms.example: FileZilla uses SFTP to transfer files between your laptop and EC2

terms.definition: Secure Copy Protocol — a command-line tool for transferring files between hosts over SSH. Uses -i for key, -r for directories.
terms.example: 'scp -i key.pem file.txt ec2-user@IP:~/' to upload a file to EC2

terms.definition: A shell operator that redirects standard output from the terminal to a file. If the file doesn't exist, it is created automatically.
terms.example: 'command > output.log' saves all output to output.log instead of printing to terminal

terms.definition: The default output stream of a process — normally printed to the terminal screen. Can be redirected to a file using >.
terms.example: All download messages from yum go to stdout by default

terms.definition: Keyboard shortcut that sends a SIGINT signal to the foreground process, terminating it immediately.
terms.example: Press Ctrl+C to stop a long-running foreground process

terms.definition: Keyboard shortcut that sends a SIGTSTP signal, suspending (pausing) the foreground process and placing it in Stopped (T) state.
terms.example: Press Ctrl+Z to pause a running process, then fg or bg to resume it
